object.title: Balanced diagonal conjecture for frequency squares
object.statement:
Let $L$ be a frequency square of type $F(m\lambda;\lambda^m)$. A **balanced diagonal conjecture** asserts that if $(m-1)\lambda$ is even, then $L$ contains a balanced diagonal.

The paper establishes this for $m\in\{1,2,3\}$ and gives constructions and observations supporting the claim for $m\geqslant4$.
object.source_name: Nicholas Cavenagh and Adam Mammoliti, “Balanced diagonals in frequency squares”, arXiv:1802.01217 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.01217

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

object.title: Henning–Yeo bound for four-uniform linear hypergraphs
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a $4$-uniform linear hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, and let $\tau(H)$ be its transversal number. **Henning–Yeo conjecture.**

$$
\tau(H) \le \frac{n}{4}+\frac{m}{6}.
$$

The source presents this as a conjecture posed in earlier work; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved, so its status remains open.
object.source_name: Michael A. Henning and Anders Yeo, “Transversals in Uniform Linear Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1802.01825 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.01825

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2018). “The case $k=4$ is much more difficult than the cases $k \in \{2,3\}$, as the conjecture does not hold for general (non-linear) hypergraphs when $k=4$.”

object.title: Dimca–Sticlaru conjecture on the combinatorial freeness defect of line arrangements
object.statement:
Let $C:f=0$ be a line arrangement in $\mathbb{P}^2$, and let $\nu(C)$ denote its freeness defect.

**Dimca–Sticlaru conjecture.** The invariant $\nu(C)$ is combinatorially determined.

This is presented as a stronger version of Terao's conjecture, and the source records that some cases are known. Its equivalent formulation in terms of the generic splitting type is merged into this row.
object.source_name: Alexandru Dimca and Gabriel Sticlaru, “Line and rational curve arrangements, and Walther's inequality”, arXiv:1803.05386 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05386

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2018).

object.title: Flip-connectivity conjecture for amplituhedron triangulations
object.statement: A **flip** replaces one of the two triangulations associated with a nearly $(n,k,m)$-admissible affine permutation by the other. **Flip-connectivity conjecture.** Any two triangulations of the amplituhedron are connected by a sequence of flips. This generalizes the corresponding connectivity theorem for triangulations of cyclic polytopes; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Pavel Galashin and Thomas Lam, “Parity duality for the amplituhedron”, arXiv:1805.00600 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00600

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2018). “It is an important open problem to give a formula for $\omega_{\ampl}$ without referring to triangulations.”

object.title: Three-dimensional Polytope Translation hardness conjecture
object.statement:
Let $P
e\varnothing$ be a rational polytope in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The **Polytope Translation hardness conjecture.** The Polytope Translation problem for rational polytopes $P\subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is ${\textup{\textsf{NP}}}$-hard. This conjecture asks whether the known hardness result in dimension six can be reduced to dimension three; the source presents it as an open problem.
object.source_name: Danny Nguyen and Igor Pak, “On the number of integer points in translated and expanded polyhedra”, arXiv:1805.03685 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03685

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

object.title: Ternary Goldbach conjecture with primes in one progression modulo $3$
object.statement:
Let $p,q,r$ be primes. **The ternary progression Goldbach conjecture.** Every odd integer $n>5$ can be written as

$$
n=p+q+r,
$$

with

$$
p\equiv q\equiv2\pmod3.
$$

This is stated as a ternary analogue of one of the explicit mod-$4$ refinements. The paper notes that results for the binary case would also yield ternary consequences, but this particular progression statement remains unproved.
object.source_name: Kimball Martin, “Refined Goldbach conjectures with primes in progressions”, arXiv:1806.00946 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.00946

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

object.title: Gruenbaum–Giessen h-vector inequality for simplicial arrangements
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a simplicial arrangement in $\mathbb{P}^3$, and let $h_i^{\mathcal{A}}$ denote its $h$-vector entries.

**Gruenbaum–Giessen h-vector conjecture.** One has

$$
h_2^{\mathcal{A}} > \sum_{i \geq 3} h_i^{\mathcal{A}}.
$$

This is presented as a conjecture from Gruenbaum and Giessen. The source does not state a resolution, so the inequality remains open here.
object.source_name: David Geis, “On simplicial arrangements in P^3(R) with splitting polynomial”, arXiv:1902.11185 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

object.title: Quadratic-reduction dimension bound for $c_2$-invariants
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a primitive graph with first Betti number $h_1(G)$, and suppose its quadratic $n$-invariant ${}^n\Psi_G^2$ exists. **Quadratic-reduction dimension conjecture.** Then

$$
\dim(c_2(G))\leq 2h_1(G)-n-1.
$$

The preceding lemma supplies a model giving this type of bound; the conjectural point is that it bounds the minimal-model dimension of the $c_2$-invariant.
object.source_name: Oliver Schnetz, “Geometries in perturbative quantum field theory”, arXiv:1905.08083 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08083

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2019). “Although the conjecture is false in general , a connection between the point-counting function and the period $()$ remains valid.”

object.title: Lower-bound conjecture for type-2 zero-problem 3M-DAPs
object.statement:
Let $P=(T;U,V)$ be a 3M-DAP, with parameters $t,v,s_t,s_v,x_t,x_v$, and let $f(P)$ denote its optimal value.

**Type-2 zero-problem lower-bound conjecture.** If $(v-1)t-v>0$ and $s_t>(v-1)s_v$, then

$$
f(P)>\frac{(v-1)x_t-x_v}{(v-1)t-v}.
$$

The source says that this inequality is used to justify a structural lemma for optimal solutions, but gives no resolution in the supplied context.
object.source_name: Richard E. Chatwin, “An Optimal Solution for the Muffin Problem”, arXiv:1907.08726 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.08726

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019). “The second conjecture has been proved by Cui et al. (2018) (see Theorem 20 therein).”

object.title: Direct-product immersion conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and write $\operatorname{im}(G)=t$ and $\operatorname{im}(H)=r$. **Direct-product immersion conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{im}(G\times H)\geq (t-1)(r-1)+1.
$$
 This conjecture asserts that the direct product preserves the proposed lower bound for immersion numbers; the paper gives partial results but does not resolve the general case.
object.source_name: Karen L. Collins, Megan E. Heenehan and Jessica McDonald, “Clique immersion in graph products”, arXiv:1908.10457 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10457

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2019). “The lexicographic product is of particular interest because Catlin disproved the Haj\'os Conjecture , that is, if $\chi(G) = n$, then $G$ contains a subdivision of $K_n$, using lexicographic products of odd cycles and complete graphs.”

object.title: Classification conjecture for simple groups with a generically 4-transitive action
object.statement: Let $G$ be a simple group of finite Morley rank admitting a generically $4$-transitive action. **Generically 4-transitive classification conjecture.** Either $G\simeq\operatorname{PGL}_3$ or $G\simeq E_6$. This is a proposed high-transitivity special case of the broader classification programme; the survey presents it as open.
object.source_name: Alexandre Borovik and Adrien Deloro, “Binding groups, permutations groups and modules of finite Morley rank”, arXiv:1909.02813 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.02813

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

object.title: Uniqueness of code-loop representations by degree and type
object.statement: Let $L$ be a code loop, and let $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ be representations of $L$. The **degree-and-type uniqueness conjecture.** If $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ have the same degree and type, then they are isomorphic. The claim is motivated by the fact that, for code loops of ranks 3 and 4, the type determines the loop up to isomorphism; whether the analogous uniqueness holds in general is left open.
object.source_name: Rosemary Miguel Pires, Alexandre Grishkov and Marina Rasskazova, “Representations of code loops by binary codes”, arXiv:1909.05143 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05143

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

object.title: The degree-zero word-map conjecture on GL2 modulo its center
object.statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $w(x_1,\dots,x_m)$ be a group word whose degree in each variable $x_i$ is $0$, and set $G={\rm GL}_2(K)/\{\pm 1\}$. **Degree-zero word-map conjecture.** The image of $w$ on $G$ is ${\rm PSL}_2(K)$. This is presented as a reformulation of the surjectivity conjecture for ${\rm PSL}_2$; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Alexei Kanel-Belov, Sergey Malev, Louis Rowen and Roman Yavich, “Evaluations of Noncommutative Polynomials on Algebras: Methods and Problems, and the L'vov-Kaplansky Conjecture”, arXiv:1909.07785 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.07785

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2019). “The most challenging open problem for word maps on semisimple algebraic groups is the following, see :”

object.title: Duality conjecture for strongly pigeonhole classes of matroids
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a strongly pigeonhole class of matroids. **Duality conjecture.** The class $\{M^{*}\colon M\in\mathcal{M}\}$ is strongly pigeonhole. The preceding result establishes the analogous claim for pigeonhole classes, but the strongly pigeonhole case is left open.
object.source_name: Daryl Funk, Dillon Mayhew and Mike Newman, “Tree automata and pigeonhole classes of matroids: I”, arXiv:1910.04360 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04360

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

object.title: Undecidability conjecture for rank-3 gain-graphic matroids
object.statement: Let $H$ be an infinite group, and consider the class of rank-$3$ **$H$-gain-graphic matroids**. **Undecidability conjecture.** This class has an undecidable ${\mathit{MS}_{0}}$ theory. The source presents this as a belief rather than a proved result; it follows the preceding discussion of the unresolved finite-exponent case for infinite groups.
object.source_name: Daryl Funk, Dillon Mayhew and Mike Newman, “Tree automata and pigeonhole classes of matroids: I”, arXiv:1910.04360 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04360

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

object.title: Efficient pigeonhole conjecture for bicircular and gain-graphic matroids
object.statement: Let $H$ be a finite group. **Efficient pigeonhole conjecture.** The class of bicircular matroids is efficiently pigeonhole, and the class of $H$-gain-graphic matroids is efficiently pigeonhole. The surrounding discussion presents these as conjectures about classes for which efficient pigeonhole structure is expected; no resolution is supplied in the paper excerpt.
object.source_name: Daryl Funk, Dillon Mayhew and Mike Newman, “Tree automata and pigeonhole classes of matroids: II”, arXiv:1910.04361 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04361

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

object.title: Vega's wedge-of-spheres conjecture for matching complexes of caterpillar graphs
object.statement: Let $G$ be a caterpillar graph, and let $M_k(G)$ denote its $k$-matching complex. **Vega's conjecture.** The $k$-matching complex $M_k(G)$ is either contractible or homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres. This conjecture extends the known result for $1$-matching complexes of forests and Vega's results for $2$-matching complexes of perfect caterpillar graphs; the general case remains open.
object.source_name: Anurag Singh, “Bounded degree complexes of forests”, arXiv:1910.12793 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.12793

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

object.title: Fraughnaugh and Locke's 2-connectivity conjecture for triangle-free subcubic graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a $2$-connected triangle-free subcubic graph on $n$ vertices. **Fraughnaugh and Locke's conjecture.**

$$
\alpha(G)\geq \frac{3}{8}n-\frac{1}{4}.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the known lower bounds for connected triangle-free subcubic graphs by imposing $2$-connectivity. The source gives no resolution status for this conjecture.
object.source_name: Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Jan Goedgebeur and Gwenaël Joret, “Large independent sets in triangle-free cubic graphs: beyond planarity”, arXiv:1911.12471 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.12471

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2019). “This was first conjectured by Albertson, Bollob\'as and Tucker, and was later proved by Heckman and Thomas.”

object.title: The Shortest Cycle Cover Conjecture
object.statement:
For a bridgeless graph $G$, let $scc(G)$ denote the length of a shortest cycle cover of $G$. **Shortest Cycle Cover Conjecture.** If $G$ is a bridgeless graph, then

$$
scc(G)\leq \frac{7}{5}|E(G)|.
$$

This conjecture gives a sharp proposed upper bound for shortest cycle covers and is related in the paper to the parameter $T(G)$. It remains open.
object.source_name: Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “Expanding vertices to triangles in cubic graphs”, arXiv:2504.19201 (2025).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2004.14049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.14049).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19201

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

object.title: Packing coloring conjecture for (3,0)-saturated subcubic graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a $(3,0)$-saturated subcubic graph, and let $g_3(G)$ denote its local girth parameter. **Packing coloring conjecture.** If

$$
g_3(G)=3,
$$

then $G$ is $(1,1,2)$-packing colorable. The paper proves $(1,1,2,4)$-packing colorability in this setting and reports no example that fails the stronger three-color assertion; it remains open.
object.source_name: Ayman El Zein and Maidoun Mortada, “Impact of local girth on the S-packing coloring of k-saturated subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2603.25113 (2026).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2408.12189](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12189), [arXiv:2404.09337](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09337), [arXiv:2011.02175](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02175).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25113

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).
